reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: This is a radiation therapy trial targeting residual tumor cells. No biomarker data is available to confirm target engagement, but stereotactic radiosurgery by design delivers high-dose focused radiation to the target tissue. The dose range of 15-22 Gy is within standard therapeutic ranges for brain metastases. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers were measured. The mechanism is DNA damage leading to cell death in residual tumor cells. Without biomarker data, we cannot confirm downstream biological changes. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint of Local Control at 1 year was met. The trial reports 13/39 patients achieved local control (33.3%), with additional data showing 23/39 patients achieved no evidence of disease (59.0%). Only 2/39 patients had progression (5.1%) and 1/39 had relapse (2.6%). This suggests clinical benefit was achieved. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: This was a single-arm trial in patients with brain metastases from various solid tumors. No subgroup analyses were reported that would suggest differential responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This is a single-arm Phase II trial without a control group, which limits the strength of evidence. However, the local control rate appears reasonable for this indication and the safety profile was manageable with mostly low-grade adverse events.

failure_modes.evidence: Single-arm trial design without control group limits ability to definitively attribute efficacy to treatment. No biomarker data available to confirm target engagement or pathway modulation.
